notes.title: Thrust is cheap. Controlled thrust is the whole job.
notes.body: Shipping a demo is thrust. Keeping it upright in production is trust.

notes.title: I sit on both sides of the table.
notes.body: In the room with clients and executives for the readout, the scope and the sign-off; back in the code for the hard parts. Nothing is lost in translation, because there is no translation.

notes.title: I own systems from the first drawing to the runbook.
notes.body: The architecture, the product, the safety layer, the release, and the team that builds it. The same hands write a Rust power API, a guarded SQL agent and a Terraform module.

notes.title: Most of the work sits in the unglamorous middle.
notes.body: Orchestration, the schema that refuses bad data, the job queue that survives a restart.

notes.title: Decisions are written down.
notes.body: Decision records, specs, runbooks and handoff notes ship with the code, so the next team starts where I stopped.

notes.title: Numbers come with their conditions.
notes.body: When a figure appears in one of my READMEs, a results file sits behind it.

notes.title: AI where it earns its place.
notes.body: When a saved answer or a plain rule will do, no model is called. Everything else fails loud.
